Chapter 2
Literature Review
2.1
Introduction
The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing
(NLP) has significantly improved intelligent information retrieval systems. Traditional
keyword-based search engines rely on lexical matching, which often fails to capture the
semantic meaning of user queries. Recent developments in semantic search and Large
Language Models (LLMs) have enabled more intelligent and context-aware retrieval sys-
tems.
This chapter reviews the technologies and research areas relevant to the proposed
Intelligent Research Assistant.
2.2
Large Language Models
Large Language Models (LLMs) are deep learning models trained on massive text corpora
to understand and generate natural language. Models such as GPT, LLaMA, Mistral,
Gemini, and Claude have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in answering questions,
summarizing documents, translating languages, and generating code.
Despite their impressive performance, LLMs suffer from certain limitations:
• Hallucination of facts
• Limited knowledge after training
• Lack of source attribution
• Difficulty incorporating private documents
These limitations motivate the integration of retrieval mechanisms with language
models.
